newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans turn firm on Refco, Smith Barney buy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans turn firm on Refco, Smith Barney buy.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures turned firmer early as commercial selling waned which left the market vulnerable to a recovery when Refco Inc and Smith Barney turned to the buy side in the March, traders said.
"It's pretty impressive. When the commercial selling stopped there wasn't anything more for sale," a trader said.
Traders said Cargill Inc and ADM Investor Services each sold one million bushels of March on the open with that action tied to hedge selling of producer and/or elevator stocks.
Refco Inc and Smith Barney each had bought roughly one half million bushels of March as of 1000 CST.
Soybeans were pressured early on forecasts for rain this weekend in the key Brazilian soybean region of Rio Grande do Sul, the traders said.
But the market remained underpinned by Friday's USDA cut in its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks and on uncertainty about the fate of the South American soybean crop.
At 1002 CST, soybeans were 1/2 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with January up 2-1/4 at $7.35. March was up 1-1/4 at $7.38.
